answer.origin: Third-party relay: Investing.com article (republished on Yahoo Finance AU, published 2026-07-22) reporting BofA Research's characterization of AMD's own estimates. No AMD primary document was supplied, and no statement date for AMD's estimates was disclosed.
answer.note: Source claim: BofA, as relayed by the media article, says AMD estimates its EPYC 9965 (Turin) delivers about 2.4x the rack-level throughput of NVIDIA's Vera baseline in a modeled 100kW deployment, and that the next-generation EPYC 6 (Venice) is projected at about 3.3x total throughput. This is a vendor's modeled estimate of a competitor's baseline, passed through two intermediaries, so it supports only a conditional conclusion. If the modeled throughput advantage holds under comparable conditions, it pressures NVIDIA's positioning of Vera as a rack-level CPU alongside Rubin, since it frames the contest around concurrency and service density rather than per-thread latency. The figures do not measure Vera against EPYC in an independent test, do not show NVIDIA's customer wins or lost orders, and do not show that buyers will adopt AMD's metric. The 3.3x figure is a projection for a product not yet shipping and is weaker than the 2.4x figure.
limitations: The workload definition, model assumptions and Vera baseline configuration behind the 2.4x and 3.3x figures are not disclosed, so the figures cannot be compared with NVIDIA's own performance claims.
The figures are AMD estimates as characterized by BofA; no AMD primary document or methodology was supplied, and the article's paraphrase may not match AMD's wording.
The date of AMD's estimates is not stated; the article's publication date does not supply a statement date.
The EPYC 6 (Venice) projection is forward-looking and describes an unreleased product, so no shipped-product evidence supports it.
follow_up: Retrieve AMD's AI 2026 Day materials and any published methodology for the 100kW rack-throughput model to confirm the 2.4x and 3.3x figures and their workload and baseline definitions.
Check whether NVIDIA has published rebuttal or comparable rack-level throughput data for Vera against EPYC configurations.
Once Vera systems ship, look for independent third-party benchmarks of agentic or concurrency workloads on Vera versus EPYC 9965 under disclosed configurations.
Confirm whether BofA's own note contains these figures and the exact attribution, since only the media relay was supplied.
